title: Guarantees of the almost-wise independent construction
statement: Let $k,n,a,b$ be natural numbers with $1\le k\le n$, $a>0$, and $2a\le b$. Set $d=\max(1,\lceil\log_2 n\rceil)$, $r=\lceil b/a\rceil$, $s=k(d+1)$, $q=sr$, and $t=\lceil nb/a\rceil$, where the ceilings of rational quantities are rounded up to natural numbers. For the construction with these parameters, let $L$ be its output list, let $M$ be the cardinality of its output multiset, let $W$ be its construction work, and let $B=2d$ be its random-bit count. Then $0<a/b\le 1/2$, $|L|=M=2^B$, $M\le16(s/(a/b))^2$, and $M\le4q^2$. As $s/(a/b)$ tends to infinity along such inputs, $M=O((s/(a/b))^2)$; as $q$ tends to infinity, $M=O(q^2)$. The construction's probability density, transferred to the sign cube, has every nonempty Fourier coefficient on at most $k$ coordinates bounded in absolute value by $a/b$. Also, $B\le2(\lceil\log_2 k\rceil+\lceil\log_2(d+1)\rceil+\lceil\log_2 r\rceil)$, and $B$ is $O(\lceil\log_2 k\rceil+\lceil\log_2(d+1)\rceil+\lceil\log_2 r\rceil)$ as that quantity tends to infinity. The work is the sum of the Vandermonde construction work and the small-bias construction work, plus $2^B$ times the matrix-vector multiplication work per output; it is at most $2^{38}(t+1)^{16}$ and is $O((t+1)^{16})$ as $t$ tends to infinity.
